_comment: Curated layer for the `surface` section of docs/capabilities.json (discoverability-design.md, stapel-catalog sweep). NOTE the honest boundary: capabilities.json itself is otherwise still HAND-WRITTEN (authored in the stapel-catalog sweep, commit 1c69898) — no gate registry, no codegen step deriving axes/extension_points from code. `make contract` patches in the two derivable things: module/version from pyproject and the derived `surface`. surface_roots deliberately EXCLUDE models.py's signal receivers (copy_parent_features, emit_category_changed_on_*save — the bus/ORM calls those, not a product), events.py's publish_category_changed (called only from those same signal receivers, never meant to be called directly) and functions.py's features_function (a stapel-core comm Function dispatched by name via call('categories.features', ...) — its own module docstring says 'no import of this package needed', the opposite of usage surface). What remains is the actual call-this-instead-of-writing-your-own surface: the feature-editor engine, the catalog fixture-sync engine, and the translation-key/display-label helpers.

build_editor_state.intent: Build the feature-editor's read-model JSON for a category (own + inherited features, per-slug available_actions, available root features, echoed revision) in one call — the shape the editor UI/API is built on. Recomputing it by hand means re-deriving the M-4 rule that edit/remove are only offered for a slug the parent does NOT carry.

apply_feature_editor_changes.intent: Apply a batch of feature-editor actions (keep/add/edit/inherit/remove/create/replace) to a category and propagate to descendants, under an optimistic-concurrency lock — call this instead of writing your own upsert/propagate loop over Category/Feature/CategoryFeature, which would have to re-derive the M-5 subtree row-lock + revision check, the M-4 inherited-slug rule and the L-9/L-11 replace/inherit consistency rules from scratch. Raises FeatureEditorError (400, rule violation) or FeatureEditorConflict (409, stale base_revision).
instead_of: a hand-written Category/Feature/CategoryFeature upsert-and-propagate loop without the M-5 select_for_update lock or the M-4/L-9/L-11 rule checks

validate_features.intent: Reject a category that carries two features sharing the same root (two versions of one inherited feature the host must pick between) — call this from wherever a category's feature set is validated (Category.clean() already does) instead of writing your own root-collision scan over category.features.
instead_of: a hand-rolled scan for duplicate root_pk across category.features

feature_warnings.intent: Collect the non-blocking findings only a category's WHOLE resolved feature set can answer: a rule condition, or a ref-type's optionsRef.parentFeature, naming a slug no feature in the category defines. Reach for it when reviewing or importing a category schema. It never raises — the same feature is reused across categories with different field sets, where an unknown controlling slug legitimately reads as empty — so treat the result as review material, not a gate.
instead_of: reading FeatureDef.rules by hand to work out which controlling slugs a category actually defines

canonical_json.intent: Byte-stable JSON text (sorted keys, no ASCII-escaping, trailing newline) for anything meant to diff cleanly across runs — a committed fixture file or a hash input. Use this instead of calling json.dumps with your own parameter choices, or the file stops being byte-identical for identical DB state.
instead_of: json.dumps(obj) with ad hoc sort_keys/indent/ensure_ascii choices

content_hash.intent: Content hash of one canonical fixture record (compact sorted-key encoding), for comparing a fixture record's identity against the DB or a previous sync-state sidecar. Use this exact hashing wherever you need two tools to agree on whether a record changed — a different key order or whitespace choice hashes differently.
instead_of: a hand-rolled hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(record)) with its own key-ordering/whitespace choices

category_sync_view.intent: A category record as the 3-way catalogue sync sees it: the presentation keys (catalog_icon/carousel_icon/carousel_enabled — stand-owned curation, see PRESENTATION_KEYS) stripped before hashing. Apply this to a category record before content_hash wherever a tool must agree with export/load about whether the record changed; hashing the full record reads an operator's carousel edit as catalogue drift.
instead_of: content_hash(record) over the full category record, which disagrees with the sidecar's category hashes

build_catalog.intent: Snapshot the live Category/Feature/CategoryFeature tables into the natural-key fixture shape (features/categories/sync-state sidecar) — call this for any export/dump/diff tooling that needs the catalog as portable JSON, instead of re-deriving the is_test exclusion, soft-delete filtering and nearest-exported-ancestor parent_slug resolution by hand.

find_orphan_overrides.intent: Detect override Feature rows (tn_parent set) linked to zero live categories — the check an ops/audit job should branch on to flag leaked override rows before they accumulate. Read-only: it reports, it does not clean up (catalog_load's own cleanup runs during a load, not from here).

load_catalog.intent: Reconcile a directory of catalog fixtures into the live DB via a 3-way diff (base=sidecar, theirs=fixture, ours=DB) — the engine behind `manage.py load_catalog`. Call it directly from a deploy script or a data-migration when you need the identical semantics (idempotent re-load, is_test invisibility, subtree row-lock, conflict policy) instead of writing your own fixture-to-DB upsert loop. Rows are matched by source identity (external_source, external_id) before slug, so a source-side rename updates in place instead of duplicating the node.
instead_of: a hand-written fixture-to-DB upsert loop using bulk_create()/QuerySet.update() (skips the revision bump, category.changed emit and full_clean() validation Model.save() gives you)

active_under_inactive_parent.intent: Slugs of ACTIVE categories whose parent is INACTIVE — a category a seller can reach by search or a saved link while the path to it is closed. Branch on this to catch a RESURRECTION: `active` is stand-owned curation the loader writes only on create, so a re-import cannot undo a deactivation, but a queryset .update(), an older release or a hand edit can; this asserts the shape such a write produces rather than the event. A subtree retired from the top answers empty.

dead_end_leaves.intent: Slugs of ACTIVE, non-deleted leaf categories with zero features (own + inherited, resolved with Category.get_all_features — the same logic the product renders with): pickable dead ends that type nothing. Branch on this in health/gate tooling instead of re-deriving leaf-ness and inheritance by hand; the catalog_health command turns a non-empty answer into a non-zero exit, and load_catalog stamps it onto its report.

identity_translator.intent: The null DISPLAY_TRANSLATOR (returns the key unchanged) — reach for this to explicitly reset or bypass translation (tests, a raw-key admin view) instead of writing your own passthrough.

translate.intent: Render one translation key through the configured DISPLAY_TRANSLATOR seam, with the None/empty-key guard already applied. Call this, not `categories_settings.DISPLAY_TRANSLATOR(key)` directly — the raw seam has no guard and breaks on a falsy key.

get_feature_key.intent: The exact cache key for a feature's memoized admin display label (per feature + active language) — use this wherever you read or invalidate that cache entry, so a custom invalidation path can't drift from the key cache_feature_translation writes under.

translate_feature.intent: The cached admin display label for a feature (depth marker, id path, mandatory star, type, config summary), built lazily on a cache miss — call this anywhere a feature needs its formatted admin label instead of re-deriving the label format or bypassing the cache.
instead_of: re-deriving the '<depth-marker><id-path><*> - <caption> [<type>](<summary>)' label format by hand

cache_feature_translation.intent: Force-rebuild and re-cache a feature's admin display label — call this after a change translate_feature's own cache would not know to invalidate (e.g. a bulk update that bypasses Feature.save()), instead of leaving a stale cached label around.

collect_category_translation_keys_with_r.intent: Every category translation key in tree-walk order, each with its admin refs and hierarchical comment — the manifest a translation-catalog export/dump tool should build from, instead of re-walking the category tree by hand.

collect_category_translation_keys.intent: Just the set of category translation keys (no refs/comments) — for a cheap completeness/diff check against a translation catalog when you don't need the full collect_category_translation_keys_with_refs manifest.

collect_feature_translation_keys_with_re.intent: Every feature translation key (name + config UI keys + option labels) in tree-walk order with admin refs/comments — use this, not a naive tree-walk, since it already knows to descend into polymorphic config option labels (select/hierarchical_select) that a generic walk would miss.
instead_of: a hand-written feature tree-walk that reads only feature.name and misses config option-label keys

collect_feature_translation_keys.intent: Just the set of feature translation keys — for a lightweight completeness check without building the full refs/comments manifest.

collect_all_catalog_translation_keys.intent: Categories and features combined into one manifest (deduplicated all_keys + total_count) — the one call a translation-catalog completeness/dump tool needs instead of running and merging the four collect_*_translation_keys* calls itself.
